title: The same source code line can correspond to multiple instruction ranges and identification numbers.
summary: The DWARF line number program records the mapping of addresses to source locations; the discriminator is used to distinguish multiple code blocks at the same source code location.
applies: Native program crash reporting and DWARF debugging metadata
detail: A certain source code line can contain branches or inline expansions, and the same file and line numbers are allowed to appear repeatedly on multiple machine addresses.
boundary: Only the line number cannot uniquely restore a certain machine instruction, nor can all events with the same line number be directly counted as one execution. See DWARF 5 §6.2.
relevance: Avoid mistaking different basic blocks for the same location when merging profiling or crash records.
